examples.question_text: Find the midpoint of the horizontal interval joining $A(-5,2)$ and $B(4,2)$.
Find the midpoint of the vertical interval joining $P(2,-4)$ and $Q(2,3)$.
Find the midpoint of the interval joining $A(-9,6)$ and $B(4,-11)$.
examples.solution_text:
Average the two $x$-coordinates, then the two $y$-coordinates.
$\begin{aligned}\overline{x}&=\frac{-9+4}{2}\\&=-2.5\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}\overline{y}&=\frac{6+(-11)}{2}\\&=-2.5\end{aligned}$
$M=(-2.5,-2.5)$.

methods.description: Average corresponding endpoint coordinates and write the midpoint as an ordered pair. Horizontal and vertical intervals retain their shared coordinate; negative values and half-integer results use the same method.

examples.derivation: The graph gives A(-2,1) and B(4,5). The coordinate means are (-2+4)/2=1 and (1+5)/2=3, giving M=(1,3). The solution marker lies halfway along AB.
The shared y-coordinate is 2. The x-coordinate mean is (-5+4)/2=-0.5, giving M=(-0.5,2). All three diagram points lie on the horizontal interval, with M halfway between the endpoints.
The shared x-coordinate is 2. The y-coordinate mean is (-4+3)/2=-0.5, giving M=(2,-0.5). The solution diagram places M halfway along the vertical interval.
The coordinate means are (-9+4)/2=-2.5 and (6+(-11))/2=-2.5, giving M=(-2.5,-2.5). Explicit endpoint coordinates make a diagram unnecessary.
